rationale: The source describes a desired change (lazy provider imports to cut startup cost), not a malfunction. Research must first verify the premise — that providers really are imported eagerly — then map every import path, the optional-dependency story in pyproject.toml, and the public API surface that a lazy scheme must preserve.

queries.intent: Read the package entrypoint to see what notify/__init__.py imports at import time
Read the Notify factory to understand current provider dispatch and the PROVIDERS registry
List every provider package to size the eager-import surface
Find eager imports of concrete providers anywhere in the package (the premise under test)
Detect any existing dynamic/lazy import machinery already in the codebase
Check whether provider modules guard third-party imports with try/except ImportError
Determine which provider dependencies are hard requirements vs optional extras
Inspect the providers package __init__ for an eager registry or re-export block
Read ProviderBase to learn the contract a lazy loader must still satisfy
Identify third-party top-level imports inside provider modules that dominate import cost
Find public API re-exports users may rely on (Notify, providers, models) that lazy loading must preserve
Check how the notify server / wrapper resolves providers, since it may bypass the factory
Find tests that import providers directly and would constrain or detect a lazy refactor
Measure the real cost: which imports dominate `import notify` wall time today
Check recent activity on the factory and providers package for in-flight refactors
Check recent activity on the providers tree for in-flight refactors
Look for documented provider-installation / extras guidance that a lazy scheme must match
See whether setup.py participates in packaging providers or extras

expected_findings: Whether notify/__init__.py (or notify/providers/__init__.py) imports concrete providers eagerly
Whether the Notify factory already lazily imports via importlib and what PROVIDERS caches
The count of provider packages and their third-party top-level imports
Whether provider deps are hard requirements or optional extras in pyproject.toml
Whether missing dependencies currently raise at import time or at Notify() call time
Public API surface (__all__, re-exports) a lazy scheme must preserve
Test coverage that would break or detect the refactor
